rv.q: Their cost comes across powerfully in Michael Longhurst’s fluid production, which has a stunning set by Es Devlin that calls to mind a space-age cosmetics counter. Karla Crome is especially good as the combative Alice, while Amy Beth Hayes perfectly evokes the predatory cunning of Amy.
Skinner's play, which starts so promisingly, ends by making Linda seem a victim of hapless circumstance rather than a tragic archetype.
Despite the modish predictability of all this, Skinner is plumbing an authentic subject in the representation, and sexualisation, of women in a superficial, appearance-obsessed society.
Despite some good satirical points, and some good jokes, Skinner takes the temperature of the times with a rather insensitive thermometer, one which is frustratingly unsubtle.

cn.t: Penelope Skinner's play about ageism and female invisibility starts strong but ultimately undermines its own message, though Noma Dumezweni earns praise for heroically stepping into the lead role at short notice.
